newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Metroplex says to focus on hotel, leisure.
newsitem.headline: Metroplex says to focus on hotel, leisure.

text.p: Malaysia's Metroplex Bhd said on Thursday it plans to focus on hotel and leisure activities under a proposed restructuring plan.
Its main property development subsidiaries will be disposed of to a new investment holding company called Newco, Metroplex said in a statement.
Metroplex plans to hive off four of its property development subsidiaries to Newco, which will also absorb six other private development companies owned by Metroplex.
Newco will buy the six private firms from Metroplex for 179.2 million ringgit, the statement said.
Newco will be controlled by Metroplex's controlling shareholders and plans to be listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
The exercise will bring in cash proceeds of about 300 million ringgit to Metroplex and reduce borrowings, the company said.
Newco will pay for the deal with a rights issue of 120.12 million shares at about 2.45 ringgit each.
This will be followed by a restricted offer of shares to shareholders of Metroplex at a ratio of one Newco share for every nine existing Metroplex shares.

Newco plans to issue of 14.138 million shares for its proposed listing, while Metroplex shareholders will offer for sale the rights to 11.767 million Newco shares to Bumiputra (ethnic Malay) investors.
The planned restructuring is subject to regulatory approval and approval from Metroplex shareholders.
